draft.title: Director, Museum of Archaeology & Ethnology
draft.position_summary: The position, Director, Museum of Archaeology and Ethnology is a combined managerial, curatorial, and public relations role responsible for SFU’s archaeological and ethnographic collections and their presentation to the public and the University community. The Director provides vision and leadership for the Museum of Archaeology and Ethnology and oversees all museum programmes and operations including management of the Museum budget. The incumbent develops and implements the Museum’s five year plan in concert with that of the Department of Archaeology. This includes setting priorities, policies, and procedures, in accordance with international professional, scholarly, and ethical standards. The Director manages, conserves, and enlarges the Museum’s assets through interaction with public donors, staff in University Advancement, Office of the VP Academic, Office of Aboriginal Peoples, SFU Art Galleries, and the Library, as well as university faculty, staff, students, and members of the general public. The Director oversees the activities of museum staff, researchers, research associates, volunteers, work study students, interns, student assistants, and others who use Museum collections and resources. In doing this the Director ensures these individuals are working in compliance with international conventions, federal and provincial legislation, and University policies and procedures. The Director enhances the Museum’s and the University’s community engagement by establishing and maintaining a network of internal and external contacts and providing advice to small community museums.

model.title: Director, Museum of Archaeology and Ethnology
model.position_summary: Provides strategic leadership and overall management for SFU’s Museum of Archaeology and Ethnology, overseeing acquisition, conservation, exhibition, and public engagement of archaeological and ethnographic collections. The role develops and implements the museum’s five‑year strategic plan in alignment with the Department of Archaeology, secures funding, ensures compliance with international conventions and provincial/federal legislation, and fosters partnerships with internal university units, Indigenous communities, donors, and heritage organizations. By directing staff, volunteers, students and researchers, the Director enhances the museum’s educational, research and community‑outreach mission while maintaining the highest standards of collection care and ethical stewardship.

duties.statement: Engage community partners and the public through outreach, exhibitions and digital communications.
how_why: Liaise with senior university officials, collectors, contract archaeologists, donors, funding institutions, media and external cultural organizations at local, provincial, national and international levels.
Represent the museum as a leader in heritage management, inclusive collection care and innovative interpretation.
Research, develop and install exhibitions within the museum gallery and promote visits by scholars, school groups and community audiences.
Manage digital channels including social media, the museum website and internal SFU communications.
Develop and maintain a network of internal and external contacts in the collector, heritage and museum communities to enlist support for museum programmes.

decision_making: Develops and implements the museum’s five‑year strategic plan.
Allocates budgetary resources and approves funding proposals.
Sets policies and procedures for collection care, acquisition and access.
Approves acquisition, deaccession and loan decisions.
Selects external funding opportunities and oversees grant applications.
problem_solving: Addresses complex compliance issues related to heritage legislation and international conventions.
Resolves conservation challenges for diverse archaeological and ethnographic materials.
Navigates funding constraints while maintaining program quality.
Mediates stakeholder expectations in community outreach and partnership development.
Manages risk and security concerns for high‑value collections.

qualifications.text: Comprehensive knowledge of UNDRIP, the Truth and Reconciliation Commission Report and Calls to Action, and professional ethical obligations related to repatriation
Familiarity with international museum standards and conventions (e.g., ICOM Code of Ethics, CITES)
Excellent oral, written and presentation communication skills
Commitment to employment equity and respect for Indigenous territories and cultures
